top_categories.workout_context: 79ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Firenze's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.

Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Firenze. Practice on paved — Italian provincial and urban roads: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 83 miles.
At mile 60 of 83, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
At Gran Fondo Firenze, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Firenze. Train it until it feels boring.
6,562ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
6,562ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 83 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Firenze. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 6,562ft of climbing on paved — Italian provincial and urban roads does to your power file on race day.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on paved — Italian provincial and urban roads can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Firenze’s 83 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Gran Fondo Firenze rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on paved — italian provincial and urban roads to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and Road Specific to prepare you for 83 miles of paved — italian provincial and urban roads in Florence, Tuscany, Italy.
